rv.q: But the significance of these is brief and the darkness dissipates in the face of so much fun and froth.
Ultimately what we’re left with is the taste of love games that can all too easily become bittersweet.
It’s the more serious bits where it struggles.
While this production has both style and substance, the lack of chemistry between its lovers leaves a sour aftertaste.
Walker’s direction is a masterclass in smooth storytelling.

When the Messenger observes that Beatrice is clearly annoyed with Benedick, “The gentleman is not in your books,” her stinging response, “An he were, I would burn my study” gets a huge laugh as opposed to the more customary ripple of amusement.
In Pippa Nixon’s Beatrice and Ken Nwosu’s Benedick, it gives us one of the most charming accounts of Shakespeare’s sparring partners this decade.

cn.t: Walker's stylish, summery production delights with sparkling chemistry between Nixon's Beatrice and Nwosu's Benedick, though some find tonal inconsistencies. Critics praise the romcom energy and visual elegance while noting it doesn't always hit the mark.
